hook.text: In some US zip codes, only one or two insurers will write auto policies. Low competition means high prices.

buildup.text: High-crime, low-income urban areas see the fewest insurers.

discovery.text: Residents in insurance deserts pay 30-50% more than drivers in competitive markets.

twist.text: Some states created assigned risk pools—forcing insurers to cover high-risk drivers.

climax.text: Insurance deserts reveal a fundamental tension: insurers avoid unprofitable areas.

punchline.text: One insurer, sky-high prices. Insurance deserts penalize the poorest drivers.

quiz.question: What creates an insurance desert?
options: Few insurers willing to write policies in high-risk areas
